frozen_candidate_root_contribution: rAy encodes the coming of something into a percipient's apprehension — prototypically by sight, and modality-/truth-neutral (the perceived may be false, in a dream, or a non-visible fact). This single perceptual nucleus is transformed by regular, Quran-internally attested derivation: Form IV = cause-to-perceive / make-visible (show), Form VI = come into mutual sight, Form I with a predicative complement = 'regard/deem X as Y', and the nominals name the perceived-content in a modality (ru'ya = dream/vision, ra'y = settled view, ri'y = outward appearance, ra'ya l-'ayn = eye-perception). Two derivationally-bridged but semantically lexicalized sub-classes fall outside a bare perceptual gloss and cap the account: the frozen deictic interrogative a-ra'ayta(ka)/a-fa-ra'aytum ('tell me / consider / suppose'), in which the perceptual content is bleached, and Form III ri'a'/yura'una ('ostentation, doing-to-be-seen'), a moral-pragmatic specialization.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: rAy encodes the coming of something into a percipient's apprehension — prototypically by sight, and modality-/truth-neutral (the perceived may be false, in a dream, or a non-visible fact). This single perceptual nucleus is transformed by regular, Quran-internally attested derivation: Form IV = cause-to-perceive / make-visible (show), Form VI = come into mutual sight, Form I with a predicative complement = 'regard/deem X as Y', and the nominals name the perceived-content in a modality (ru'ya = dream/vision, ra'y = settled view, ri'y = outward appearance, ra'ya l-'ayn = eye-perception). Two derivationally-bridged but semantically lexicalized sub-classes fall outside a bare perceptual gloss and cap the account: the frozen deictic interrogative a-ra'ayta(ka)/a-fa-ra'aytum ('tell me / consider / suppose'), in which the perceptual content is bleached, and Form III ri'a'/yura'una ('ostentation, doing-to-be-seen'), a moral-pragmatic specialization.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: At its core the root means 'to have something become present/evident to you' — usually by seeing it with the eyes, but the same verb runs smoothly into 'realize', 'find/consider so', and 'see in a dream'. The system is regular: Form IV is 'show' (make someone see), Form VI is 'see one another', and the nouns name what is seen (a dream, an opinion, an outward look). Two offshoots have drifted into fixed meanings the plain 'perceive' does not predict: the frozen question-opener a-ra'ayta ('tell me / what do you think if...'), where nothing is actually being seen, and ri'a' ('showing off to be seen by people'). Because those two coherent sub-classes resist the bare 'perceive' account, the claim is graded MODERATE and REPRESENTATIVE rather than universal.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: rAy does NOT mean directing/aiming the gaze (that is nazar) nor the functioning visual faculty/organ (basar, 'ayn): the internal triad tara-hum yanzuruna ilayka wa-hum la yubsiruna (7:198:7:2) and arini anzur ilayka ... lan tarani (7:143:14:1) separate achieved apprehension (ra'a) from the attempt/gaze (nazar) and from working sight (absara). It is not mere conjecture (zann), contrasted at 11:27 (naraka ... bal nazunnukum), and not identical to knowledge ('ilm), juxtaposed at 96:14 (alam ya'lam bi-anna llaha yara). It is NOT veridical by definition: the percipient can be wrong (fa-ra'ahu hasanan of an evil deed, 35:8:6:2; yarawnahu ba'idan wa-narahu qariban, 70:6-7). The bare root carries no moral valence (ostentation is supplied only by Form III + 'to people'), does not itself encode 'dream' (that comes from fi l-manam or the noun ru'ya), and does not entail reciprocity (that requires Form VI).
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The frozen deictic idiom a-ra'aytaka(um) / a-fa-ra'aytum, most sharply at 6:40:2:2 (qul a-ra'aytakum in atakum 'adhabu llah ... a-ghayra llahi tad'un), 6:47:2:2 and 17:62:2:2 (qala a-ra'aytaka hadha lladhi karramta 'alayya). Here the perceptual content is fully bleached, the morphology is fossilized (the -ka/-kum is a frozen non-argument, invariant to sense), and the verb functions as a discourse operator 'tell me / consider / suppose' governing a conditional plus an unrelated interrogative — nothing is seen. With its 33 idiom-siblings this is the coherent resistant sub-class that blocks any STRONG/UNIVERSAL 'ra'a = perceive' claim. Secondarily, the ri'a'/yura'una ostentation class (2:264:12:1, 4:38:4:1, 8:47:8:2, 4:142:13:1, 107:6:3:1) carries a moral 'hypocritical display' surplus not recoverable from 'perceive/be-seen'.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: A two-node account: (A) ra'a = perception/apprehension (ocular -> mental 'deem' -> oneiric, with IV/VI/III as regular derivations), and (B) a grammaticalized performative frame a-ra'ayta(kum) = 'consider / inform me', better classed as an interrogative discourse particle than as a token of 'see' — on which a single 'perceive X' gloss over-generates by laundering a semantically-empty fossilized idiom into the perceptual paradigm. A stricter variant holds the core is purely visual sight and everything cognitive is metaphor. Both are kept at bay (not defeated) by Quran-internal continua: the same idiom string runs perception and cognition together (a-ra'aytum ... aruni, 46:4), 27:44 pairs saw/thought in one clause, and the 'deem' bridge is independently attested (11:27, 70:6-7, 35:8) — so node (B) and the nominals are lexicalized EXTENSIONS, not unbridged homonyms. Because the Quran cannot decisively settle whether cognitive apprehension is within the core or a metaphorical extension of a visual core, the competitor is not refuted, which is itself a reason not to grade STRONG.

internal_discovery.rationale: All three lenses converge: a genuine unified nucleus ('presence-to-a-percipient, prototypically visual') is Quran-internally demonstrable and yields sharp negative boundaries against nazar, basar, zann and 'ilm (7:198, 7:143, 11:27, 96:14). The productive verbal system (Form I core ~237, IV 40, VI 2) and most nominals sit cleanly under it, with the IV<->I bridge made explicit in one clause (ma urikum illa ma ara, 40:29). STRONG is disqualified by the contract because two coherent resistant lexicalized sub-classes exist: the fossilized a-ra'ayta(ka) discourse idiom (34 occ, ~10% of the root, perceptual content bleached) and the Form III ri'a'/rа'а ostentation class (5 occ, moral-pragmatic specialization); a lexicalized nominal (ru'ya, dream) is a milder secondary resistance. Per the rule 'a resistant lexicalized/nominal class caps strength at MODERATE and scope at REPRESENTATIVE'. UNRESOLVED is not warranted because every sub-class is derivationally bridged (idiom from 'have you seen -> considered'; ri'a' from Form III 'make-oneself-seen-by'; nominals as products of the perceptual act) — there is no unbridged homonym forcing a partition. Net: PREFERRED / MODERATE / REPRESENTATIVE.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Form I ra'a/yara = 'apprehend something as present/evident', the productive nucleus. One continuum, not a fault line: achieved visual perception (ra'a kawkaban/l-qamar/l-shams 6:76-78, ra'a naran 20:10:2:1, ra'aw l-'adhab 10:54:14:1); predicative 'regard/deem X as Y' (mа naraka illa basharan 11:27, fa-ra'ahu hasanan 35:8:6:2, ma urikum illa ma ara 40:29:21:1); reflective/cognitive alam tara / a-wa-lam yaraw apprehending even non-witnessed events or non-visible facts (alam tara kayfa fa'ala rabbuka bi-ashabi l-fil 105:1, alam tara anna llaha ya'lam 58:7:2:1); dream-frame ra'aytu ... fi l-manam (12:4, 37:102); and passive 'be seen' (sawfa yura 53:40). Modality-/truth-neutral; grounds in observation at its physical end.

clusters.supporting_evidence_note: Adversarially clean center; the nazar/basar boundary (7:198:7:2, 7:143:14:1) and zann/'ilm boundary (11:27, 96:14) give sharp external contrast.

A grammaticalized discourse operator: the perceptual content is bleached out, and in a-ra'aytaka(um) the -ka/-kum is a pleonastic non-argument (6:40:2:2, 6:47:2:2, 17:62:2:2). It typically governs a conditional 'in' clause plus an unrelated interrogative; nothing is actually seen.

clusters.supporting_evidence_note: The pleonastic -ka in 6:40/6:47/17:62 clinches fossilization: the pronoun cannot be an object yet the form is invariant, so the perceptual valence is dead.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Form IV ara = causative of Form I: 'cause to perceive / make-visible / show'. Objects are typically ayat/signs (sanurihim ayatina 41:53:1:2, nuri Ibrahima malakut 6:75:2:1), phenomena (yurikumu l-barq 13:12/30:24), demands 'show us' (arina manasikana 2:128:10:2, arina llaha jahratan 4:153), causing perception (crow 5:31; Satan 7:27), dream-showing (8:43), passive li-yuraw a'malahum (99:6).
clusters.classification_rationale: Morphologically transparent causative; the valence shift X-sees-Y -> Z-makes-X-see-Y is made explicit within one clause at 40:29 (ma urikum illa ma ara), directly bridging IV to I.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: Uniform across all 40 occurrences; no resistant sub-class internal to Form IV.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Form VI tara'a = reciprocal 'come into mutual sight': two hosts see one another — tara'a l-jam'an (26:61:2:1), tara'ati l-fi'atan (8:48:17:1).
clusters.classification_rationale: Clean reciprocal of the Form I visual sense; fully bridged, no drift.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: Both occurrences are literal mutual visual perception of opposed groups; reinforces that reciprocity is carried by the morphology, not the bare root.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Form III verb rа'а/yura'una 'display oneself to be seen by others' (yura'una l-nas 4:142:13:1; hum yura'una 107:6:3:1) and the fixed nominal ri'a'a l-nas 'ostentation, hypocritical display' (2:264:12:1, 4:38:4:1, 8:47:8:2). The semantic weight has shifted onto pretense oriented to an audience.
clusters.classification_rationale: Derivationally transparent (mufa'ala 'make-oneself-seen-by'), so bridged, not a fresh root; but pragmatically/morally lexicalized (a pejorative 'insincerity' surplus) beyond 'perceive/be-seen'. A coherent resistant lexicalized sub-class — with the a-ra'ayta idiom, the second ground that caps strength at MODERATE.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: The moral charge is supplied by Form III + audience (l-nas), not by ra'a: strongest evidence that the root does not carry one meaning across its stems.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Nominalizations naming the perceived-content by modality: ru'ya = dream/prophetic vision (12:5, 12:43x2, 12:100, 17:60, 37:105, 48:27), ra'y = settled view/opinion (badiya l-ra'y 11:27:20:2), ra'ya l-'ayn = bare eye-perception (3:13:17:1), ri'y = outward appearance/how one looks (19:74:9:2).
clusters.classification_rationale: All are products of the same apprehension act, differentiated only by modality (in-sleep / of-the-mind / of-the-eye / as-seen-from-outside); bridged to the nucleus. ru'ya (sleep/prophetic vision) and ra'y (opinion) are mild lexicalizations but remain transparent specializations, hence CONSISTENT rather than RESISTANT.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: ra'ya l-'ayn (3:13:17:1) anchors the eye-perception sense; ru'ya pairs with the oneiric Form I verb (12:4 + 12:5), confirming the noun names what the verb apprehends.

reconciliation.rationale: The alam tara frame is perception-grounded apprehension ('have you not come to realize'); it governs both physical objects (rain/crops 24:43-type) and facts, and is bridged to the ocular prototype by the same verb and construction. Cognitive apprehension is an extension of the nucleus, not a separate lexeme.

This very clause bridges IV(show)=make-see to I(see): 'I show you only what I see'. The predicative 'deem' is the perception verb taking an as-Y complement, independently attested (11:27, 70:6-7), so it stays in the perceptual nucleus.

ru'ya names the perceived-content in the sleep modality and pairs directly with the oneiric Form I verb (12:4 ra'aytu ... 12:5 ru'yaka); it is a transparent nominalization of the apprehension act, a mild lexicalization that bridges rather than a fresh root.

occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Frozen deictic interrogative a-ra'ayta / a-ra'aytum / a-ra'aytaka(um) / a-fa-ra'aytum = 'tell me / consider / what is your view if...'. A grammaticalized discourse operator: the perceptual content is bleached out, and in a-ra'aytaka(um) the -ka/-kum is a pleonastic non-argument (6:40:2:2, 6:47:2:2, 17:62:2:2). occurrence_dispositions.note: Iblis: a-ra'aytaka hadha lladhi karramta 'alayya — pleonastic -ka, deictic 'consider', no perception.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Frozen deictic interrogative a-ra'ayta / a-ra'aytum / a-ra'aytaka(um) / a-fa-ra'aytum = 'tell me / consider / what is your view if...'. A grammaticalized discourse operator: the perceptual content is bleached out, and in a-ra'aytaka(um) the -ka/-kum is a pleonastic non-argument (6:40:2:2, 6:47:2:2, 17:62:2:2). It typically governs a conditional 'in' clause plus an unrelated interrogative; nothing is actually seen.
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: The pleonastic -ka in 6:40/6:47/17:62 clinches fossilization: the pronoun cannot be an object yet the form is invariant, so the perceptual valence is dead.
occurrence_dispositions.preliminary_note: Bridged from 'have you seen -> considered' (not an unbridged homonym) but semantically lexicalized away from 'perceive' — a coherent ~10% sub-class a bare perceptual gloss does not predict; per contract this resistant lexicalized sub-class caps the account at MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE. Identified by explicit word_refs (Form I, surface ra'ayo/ra>ayo, preceded by interrogative alif a-/a-fa- in verse_text).

occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Form IV ara = causative of Form I: 'cause to perceive / make-visible / show'. occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Frozen deictic interrogative a-ra'ayta / a-ra'aytum / a-ra'aytaka(um) / a-fa-ra'aytum = 'tell me / consider / what is your view if...'. A grammaticalized discourse operator: the perceptual content is bleached out, and in a-ra'aytaka(um) the -ka/-kum is a pleonastic non-argument (6:40:2:2, 6:47:2:2, 17:62:2:2). It typically governs a conditional 'in' clause plus an unrelated interrogative; nothing is actually seen.
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: The pleonastic -ka in 6:40/6:47/17:62 clinches fossilization: the pronoun cannot be an object yet the form is invariant, so the perceptual valence is dead.

occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Nominalizations naming the perceived-content by modality: ru'ya = dream/prophetic vision (12:5, 12:43x2, 12:100, 17:60, 37:105, 48:27), ra'y = settled view/opinion (badiya l-ra'y 11:27:20:2), ra'ya l-'ayn = bare eye-perception (3:13:17:1), ri'y = outward appearance/how one looks (19:74:9:2).
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: ra'ya l-'ayn (3:13:17:1) anchors the eye-perception sense; ru'ya pairs with the oneiric Form I verb (12:4 + 12:5), confirming the noun names what the verb apprehends.

occurrence_dispositions.note: Bridged from 'have you seen -> considered' (not an unbridged homonym) but semantically lexicalized away from 'perceive' — a coherent ~10% sub-class a bare perceptual gloss does not predict; per contract this resistant lexicalized sub-class caps the account at MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE. Identified by explicit word_refs (Form I, surface ra'ayo/ra>ayo, preceded by interrogative alif a-/a-fa- in verse_text).
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Frozen deictic interrogative a-ra'ayta / a-ra'aytum / a-ra'aytaka(um) / a-fa-ra'aytum = 'tell me / consider / what is your view if...'. A grammaticalized discourse operator: the perceptual content is bleached out, and in a-ra'aytaka(um) the -ka/-kum is a pleonastic non-argument (6:40:2:2, 6:47:2:2, 17:62:2:2). independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A/B/C) converged on the same nucleus, the same two resistant sub-classes, and the same MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE grade; word_refs, forms, and the 328/237/34/40/2/5/10 partition were re-confirmed directly against the packet.
candidate_root_contribution: rAy encodes the coming of something into a percipient's apprehension — prototypically by sight, and modality-/truth-neutral (the perceived may be false, in a dream, or a non-visible fact). This single perceptual nucleus is transformed by regular, Quran-internally attested derivation: Form IV = cause-to-perceive / make-visible (show), Form VI = come into mutual sight, Form I with a predicative complement = 'regard/deem X as Y', and the nominals name the perceived-content in a modality (ru'ya = dream/vision, ra'y = settled view, ri'y = outward appearance, ra'ya l-'ayn = eye-perception). Two derivationally-bridged but semantically lexicalized sub-classes fall outside a bare perceptual gloss and cap the account: the frozen deictic interrogative a-ra'ayta(ka)/a-fa-ra'aytum ('tell me / consider / suppose'), in which the perceptual content is bleached, and Form III ri'a'/yura'una ('ostentation, doing-to-be-seen'), a moral-pragmatic specialization.

layer_attribution.occurrence_evidence: 328 occurrences read at form level (all minority forms N/N(III)/V(III)/V(VI) in full; Form I 271 and Form IV 40 across all distinct QAC surfaces). Prototype = achieved visual perception (fire, heavenly bodies, punishment, eschatological spectacle); the physical-seeing tokens are the dense, distinctive, adversarially-clean center.
layer_attribution.derivation: Regular, morphologically overt derivation from the Form I nucleus: IV = causative 'show' (bridged in-clause at 40:29), VI = reciprocal 'mutual sight', III = 'make-oneself-seen-by' (-> ostentation), and nominal patterns for the perceived-content (ru'ya/ra'y/ri'y/ra'ya l-'ayn).
layer_attribution.lexical_class: Two derivationally-bridged but lexicalized sub-classes stand apart from a bare perceptual gloss: the frozen deictic interrogative a-ra'ayta(ka)/a-fa-ra'aytum ('tell me/consider'), and Form III ri'a' ('ostentation'); ru'ya (dream) and ra'y (opinion) are milder nominal lexicalizations. These are what cap strength/scope.
layer_attribution.contextual_relation: What is seen (a shirt, a staff, stars, punishment), whom one shows off to (l-nas), or the content of a dream (eleven stars) is narrative/contextual, NOT part of the root's semantic contribution; the root supplies only the apprehension-relation, its causative/reciprocal/display transforms, and the perceived-content nominal.
layer_attribution.reconciliation: Preliminary reads that split off the cognitive alam tara, the predicative 'deem', and the ru'ya noun as separate senses were reconciled INTO the nucleus as perception-grounded extensions (bridged by shared syntax and by 40:29 show=make-see and 12:4-5 verb+noun pairing); the a-ra'ayta idiom and ri'a' class were NOT reconciled in and remain marked RESISTANT.
layer_attribution.unresolved_resistance: The 34 fossilized a-ra'ayta(ka) idioms and 5 Form III ri'a'/yura'una ostentation occurrences persist as resistant lexicalized sub-classes; additionally the Quran-internal choice between a purely-visual core (cognition = metaphor) and a broader perceptual-apprehension core is genuinely undecided — both reasons STRONG is withheld and the grade is capped at MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE.

hard_case_representation.rationale: Two coherent lexicalized sub-classes persist as genuine resistance against a bare perceptual gloss even though each is derivationally bridged: (1) the 34 fossilized a-ra'ayta(ka)/a-fa-ra'aytum deictic idioms (perceptual content bleached, morphology frozen), and (2) the 5 Form III ri'a'/yura'una ostentation occurrences (moral-pragmatic specialization). All 39 are marked RESISTANT_SEAM and appear in counterevidence_refs. A small number of ADVERSARIAL_BOUNDARY cases mark the sharp external contrasts (nazar/basar, non-veridicality) that distinguish the nucleus. This resistance is what caps the grade at MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE; it does not force UNRESOLVED because the bridges hold.

rejection_condition.challenging_finding: A subset of Form I ra'a/yara occurrences whose meaning is neither achieved perception, nor perception-grounded cognitive realization, nor the predicative 'deem X as Y', nor dream-apprehension — i.e. tokens that cannot be reduced to 'apprehension of something as being so' — OR a demonstration that the a-ra'ayta idiom and the ri'a' class do NOT bridge to the perceptual nucleus (are unrelated homonyms), which would force a multi-class/UNRESOLVED partition instead of one capped nucleus.
rejection_condition.search_location: The full Form I set (qac_verb_form=null), re-checking especially the predicative/'deem' constructions (11:27, 7:60/66, 35:8, 70:6-7, 40:29) and the alam tara / a-wa-lam yaraw reflective set for any token that is purely inferential-from-report with no evident/witnessed object; and the Form III + N(III) ostentation set (2:264, 4:38, 8:47, 4:142, 107:6) for whether 'make-oneself-seen-by' is recoverable.
rejection_condition.verification_method: For each candidate, test whether the object is presented as evident/apprehended (supports nucleus) versus merely deduced with no perceptual grounding (refutes it); and test the derivational bridge morphologically (Form III mufa'ala = 'be-seen-by'; idiom = frozen interrogative of 'see') and by parallel Quran-internal constructions.
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Do not treat contextual/narrative content (what is seen, whom one shows off to) as the root's contribution; do not let high frequency of ocular seeing launder the bleached idiom into 'perceive'; keep ra'a distinct from nazar (gaze), basar (faculty), zann (conjecture), 'ilm (knowledge) using the internal contrast verses.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If purely inferential non-perceptual Form I tokens are found, the nucleus narrows or is rejected; if the idiom/ri'a' bridges fail, research_state becomes UNRESOLVED with a multi-class partition and result_strength UNRESOLVED.

reopen_conditions: If a Quran-internal bridge is established (or refuted) between the frozen a-ra'ayta(ka) discourse idiom (6:40, 6:47, 17:62 and siblings) and the perceptual Form I nucleus — e.g. an occurrence where the idiom demonstrably retains live perceptual valence, or conversely proof it is an unrelated grammaticalized particle — reopen the idiom cluster's disposition.

If the Form III ri'a'/yura'una ostentation sense (2:264, 4:38, 8:47, 4:142, 107:6) is shown to be either fully compositional from 'make-oneself-seen-by' (removing the moral surplus, arguing for CONSISTENT) or an unbridged homonym (forcing UNRESOLVED), reopen the OSTENTATION_FORM_III grade.

If the visual-core-vs-cognitive-core question is settled by new internal evidence — e.g. an alam tara / 'deem' token that is provably purely inferential with no evident object — reopen whether cognitive apprehension is inside the nucleus or a metaphorical extension, which bears on scope.

falsification_evidence.status_rationale: A full adversarial refutation was NOT run to a clean SUPPORTED/failing_occurrences=[] verdict because genuine resistant occurrences persist (the 34-token a-ra'ayta idiom and the 5-token ri'a' class). The perceptual nucleus is distinctive (sharp nazar/basar/zann/'ilm boundaries) and holds across ~284 occurrences, but because a coherent resistant lexicalized sub-class remains, the contract requires NOT_RUN with the resisting occurrences recorded rather than PASSED.
